analysis:
Examined the two base_text units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift (lines 1264-2457). The file is a test file only. The patch excerpt shows head-side changes that are test scaffolding: a decodeTable override in the stub tokenizer, a stopStringScope parameter on the makeBridge helper, and a new scoped stop-sequence matching test (head lines ~847-899). The patch excerpt is truncated, so the test's remaining assertions are not visible. No production source is changed in the supplied evidence.

The unchanged base portions cover shared-budget KV accounting, SSD staging, cancellation, capacity mapping and receipt coverage. They exercise the T-041 controls: scoped cacheSalt, staging reservations released on every path, the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate and the retired env-var handling. They do not weaken those controls. The tests assert fail-closed behaviors: the capacity rejection leaves no leaked reservation, the staging cold fallback abandons staging, and the overflow checks reject before staging.

No new attack surface, no regression and no invalidated threat assumption were found in this test-only change. The test asserts behavior of EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence and the CBv2StopStringScope plumbing. The production change that implements them (EngineV2Bridge.swift, ReasoningStopScope) was not supplied here. A later integration pass should confirm that this production change does not alter stop-string or reasoning-scope handling in a way that leaks reasoning content (A-001) or alters billing or termination behavior. This is unverified; it is not a finding.
